items.followUp: Define energy and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Identifies that work involves a force causing displacement.
rubric.description: Work is done when a force causes displacement in its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining relationship between force and displacement.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of work and its meaning.
rubric.description: The SI unit is the joule (J); 1 J is the work done by a 1 N force moving an object 1 m in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for joule, with or without the equivalent definition.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force acting on an object causes displacement in the direction of the force.
Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force.
The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Define solar energy and wind energy.

rubric.why: Identifies biomass as energy obtained from biological material.
rubric.description: Biomass energy is energy obtained from plant and animal matter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining biomass energy as energy from biological material.

rubric.why: Identifies the Earth's internal heat as the source.
rubric.description: Geothermal energy is heat energy obtained from inside the Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining geothermal energy as energy from the Earth's interior.

modelAnswer: Biomass energy is energy obtained from plant and animal matter.
Geothermal energy is heat energy obtained from inside the Earth.

items.followUp: Define work and state the meaning of one joule.

rubric.why: States that power measures how quickly work is done.
rubric.description: Power is the rate of doing work, or work done per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining power as work per unit time.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit and its defining rate.
rubric.description: The SI unit of power is the watt (W); 1 W is one joule of work done in one second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for watt and its equivalent definition.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work, or the work done per unit time.
The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when 1 J of work is done in 1 s.

items.followUp: Derive the equation for gravitational potential energy gained by an object raised through height h.

rubric.why: Defines kinetic energy and identifies its dependence on mass and speed.
rubric.description: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or for stating the final kinetic-energy expression.

rubric.why: Connects the work done to the force and acceleration.
rubric.description: The work done on the body is W = Fs, and the force is F = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the work relation and Newton's second-law relation.

rubric.why: Uses the motion equation for a body starting from rest to obtain displacement.
rubric.description: For a body starting from rest, v² = 2as, so s = v²/(2a).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the relevant kinematic relation and displacement result.

rubric.why: Completes the derivation and states the required equation.
rubric.description: Substitution gives W = mas = ½mv²; hence kinetic energy is ½mv².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining the final equation.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
The work done to bring a body from rest to speed v is its kinetic energy.
W = Fs and F = ma, so W = mas.
For a body starting from rest, v² = u² + 2as and u = 0; therefore s = v²/(2a).
W = ma × v²/(2a) = ½mv².
Therefore, kinetic energy, KE = ½mv².

items.followUp: Derive the equation for the pressure exerted by a liquid column of height h on its base.

rubric.why: Finds the volume of the liquid column from its cross-sectional area and depth.
rubric.description: For a liquid column of area A and depth h, its volume is Ah.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the column's volume to area and depth.

rubric.why: Uses density to express the mass of the liquid column.
rubric.description: Using density ρ, the mass is m = ρV = ρAh.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly expressing the mass using density.

rubric.why: Calculates the weight of the liquid column as the force on the base.
rubric.description: The column's weight is F = mg = ρAhg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct weight/force expression.

rubric.why: Divides the force by area and obtains the pressure at depth h.
rubric.description: P = F/A = ρgh.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final pressure equation.

modelAnswer: Consider a liquid column of depth h and cross-sectional area A.
Volume of the column, V = Ah.
If the liquid density is ρ, its mass is m = ρV = ρAh.
The weight of the liquid column is F = mg = ρAhg.
Pressure at the depth is P = F/A = ρAhg/A.
Therefore, P = ρgh.

items.followUp: Differentiate between astrophysics and atomic physics.

rubric.why: Describes the application of physics to the Earth.
rubric.description: Geophysics applies the principles of physics to study the Earth and its physical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying physics as applied to the Earth or its physical properties.

rubric.why: Identifies plasma as ionized matter and the subject of plasma physics.
rubric.description: Plasma physics studies plasma, an ionized gas containing charged particles such as ions and electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the study of plasma or ionized gas.

modelAnswer: Geophysics applies the principles of physics to study the Earth and its physical properties.
Plasma physics is the study of plasma, an ionized gas containing charged particles such as ions and electrons.

items.followUp: Define velocity and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines acceleration as the change in velocity per unit time.
rubric.description: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: States the SI unit of acceleration.
rubric.description: The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared (m/s²).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
Its SI unit is metre per second squared (m/s²).

items.followUp: State Newton's first law of motion.

rubric.why: States the law in terms of the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.description: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the momentum-rate statement and its proportionality to force.

rubric.why: Includes the direction of the change or the equivalent mathematical form for constant mass.
rubric.description: The change in momentum takes place in the direction of the applied force; for constant mass, F = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the direction statement or the equivalent relation F = ma.

modelAnswer: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force.
The change in momentum takes place in the direction of the applied force.
For a body of constant mass, this law is expressed as F = ma.
